ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating Landscape Features for Cross-Task Performance Explanation
PROPOSAL: Implement a systematic evaluation protocol to compare the predictive power of various landscape features on cross-task performance. This includes studying the feature set's impact on task-specific performance, as well as the correlation between feature values across tasks. We will utilize the existing benchmarks, such as ProteinGym and RNAGym, to leverage existing data and reduce computational costs.
CONTROLS: Baseline results will be compared against the top-performing model using the current benchmarks' top-scoring metrics (e.g., average AUC-PR). Ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of each feature individually and in combinations. Controls will also include utilizing the standard open-source library and custom implementing some landscape features.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By analyzing the relationship between landscape features and cross-task performance, we can identify key feature subsets and value ranges that are predictive of task performance. We anticipate identifying patterns in landscape features that strongly correlate with high performing models, thus providing insights into the performance differences across tasks and models. However, it's unlikely that a single set of features will be predictive across all tasks and models, limiting the generalizability of our findings.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Landscape-Aware Modeling for Improved Performance Heterogeneity Understanding
PROPOSAL: We propose developing a landscape-aware modeling framework that integrates landscape features into the design and training process of ML models. This will be achieved by incorporating landscape feature-based regularizers or constraints into the model training objectives. By doing so, we can encourage the model to focus on the most informative regions of the fitness landscape and make predictions that are more consistent with the landscape's underlying structure.
CONTROLS: We will compare our landscape-aware models against their landscape-agnostic counterparts and against state-of-the-art baselines on the ProteinGym and RNAGym benchmarks. Ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of different landscape features and regularizers on model performance. Controls will also include evaluating the models' performance on different landscape metrics (e.g., ruggedness, navigability).
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging landscape features during model training, we expect to see improved model performance on tasks with complex fitness landscapes. Specifically, we anticipate that our landscape-aware models will outperform landscape-agnostic models on tasks with high epistasis and ruggedness, and achieve comparable performance on tasks with simpler landscapes. However, the improvement in performance may be limited by the quality and quantity of available landscape features, particularly for tasks with sparse or missing data.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Landscape-Aware Modeling for Improved Performance Heterogeneity Understanding
PROPOSAL: We modify our previous proposal by replacing the regularizers or constraints with a more adaptive approach. Instead of incorporating landscape features into the model training objectives, we propose using a meta-learning approach to learn a landscape-aware initialization scheme for the model parameters. By doing so, we can adapt the model's initializing weights to the specific landscape features of each task, thus improving the model's ability to generalize across different tasks and landscapes.
CONTROLS: We will compare our meta-learning approach against the original landscape-aware models and against state-of-the-art baselines on the ProteinGym and RNAGym benchmarks. Ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of different meta-learning objectives and architectural choices on model performance. Controls will also include evaluating the models' performance on different landscape metrics (e.g., ruggedness, navigability).
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging meta-learning to adapt the model's initial weights to the landscape features of each task, we expect to see improved model performance on tasks with complex fitness landscapes. Specifically, we anticipate that our meta-learning approach will outperform landscape-agnostic models on tasks with high epistasis and ruggedness, and achieve comparable performance on tasks with simpler landscapes. However, the improvement in performance may be limited by the quality and quantity of available landscape features, particularly for tasks with sparse or missing data.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Landscape Informative Feature Extraction via Variational Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: We propose using Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) to extract informative features from the landscape data. The VAE will learn a compact and meaningful representation of the landscape features, which can then be used as input to traditional ML models. By doing so, we can reduce the dimensionality of the landscape data and improve the interpretability of the models' predictions.
CONTROLS: We will compare our VAE-based approach against traditional feature extraction methods (e.g., PCA, t-SNE) and against state-of-the-art baselines on the ProteinGym and RNAGym benchmarks. Ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of different VAE architectures and hyperparameters on feature quality and model performance.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By using a VAE to extract informative landscape features, we expect to see improved model performance on tasks where the landscape data is high-dimensional and complex. Specifically, we anticipate that our VAE-based approach will outperform traditional feature extraction methods on tasks with high epistasis and ruggedness, and achieve comparable performance on tasks with simpler landscapes. However, the improvement in performance may be limited by the VAE's ability to capture non-linear relationships in the landscape data.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Multi-Task Learning for Landscape-Informed Prediction
PROPOSAL: We propose using multi-task learning to leverage the information from multiple tasks and landscapes to improve the performance on individual tasks. By sharing weights across related tasks, we can encourage the model to learn generalizable features that are informative for multiple tasks. Additionally, we will incorporate landscape features into the multi-task learning framework to further improve the model's ability to generalize across different landscapes.
CONTROLS: We will compare our multi-task learning approach against single-task learning and against state-of-the-art baselines on the ProteinGym and RNAGym benchmarks. Ablations will be performed to evaluate the impact of different multi-task learning objectives and architectural choices on model performance.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By leveraging multi-task learning and incorporating landscape features, we expect to see improved model performance on tasks with complex fitness landscapes. Specifically, we anticipate that our multi-task learning approach will outperform single-task learning models on tasks with high epistasis and ruggedness, and achieve comparable performance on tasks with simpler landscapes. However, the improvement in performance may be limited by the ability to identify related tasks and landscapes, and the effectiveness of the multi-task learning objective.
